source.title: Stop Probing, Start Coding: Why Linear Probes and Sparse Autoencoders Fail at Compositional Generalisation
source.authors: Vit'oria Barin-Pacela; S. Joshi; I. Camacho; Simon Lacoste-Julien; D. Klindt

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper text, including appendices and corrigendum, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests SAE latent recovery, dictionary learning, and downstream prediction under compositional shifts, but does not measure the SAE reconstruction residual or test any of the specified dark-matter claims.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments concern code recovery, learned dictionary quality, and task accuracy—not whether the reconstruction error is predictable from activations, how its norms scale, or whether retaining that error preserves model behavior. The rows below record adjacent SAE findings under versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study measures latent-code recovery (MCC), dictionary cosine to ground truth, support precision/recall and downstream probe accuracy for SAEs vs per-sample sparse coding under compositional shifts. It never measures the SAE reconstruction error vector, its linear predictability, per-token error norms, spliced-in loss, or behaviour lost when dropping the error term. It does not cite or engage the dark-matter paper. 'discusses' overstates the link; it neither tests nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors find an oracle dictionary solves recovery at all scales tested, and that they see scalable dictionary learning as the key open problem. They also say SAE codes never exceed raw-activation probing; on Pythia-70M the SAE ties the raw-activation probe (92.21).
record.recipe_differences: The study compares sparse-coding inference, SAE encoders, and learned dictionaries on synthetic compositional shifts and LLM activation probing; it does not use the dark-matter error-vector measurements described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with latent dimension, training data, sparsity, SAE type, and inference method. The text reports that Top-K performs better than other SAE types at smaller latent dimensions, while SAE dictionaries and dictionary-learning methods degrade at large latent dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic superposition data, SAE decoder columns point in wrong directions; norm ratios are ≈1.0. Per-sample FISTA on the frozen SAE dictionary does not close the gap to DL-FISTA (SAE ≈ frozen ≈ refined ∼0.15–0.4 ID MCC, vs DL-FISTA ∼0.75–0.95).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE failures to recover true latents stem mainly from learned dictionary directions rather than amortised encoding.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2-2B layer 12 sparse probing, mean accuracy is 95.79 for DL-FISTA, 94.63 for Top-K SAE and 95.62 for the raw-activation probe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-sample sparse inference with a learned dictionary modestly beats SAE codes on in-distribution sparse probing.

record.problems: The paper states that the real-LLM sparse-probing experiment is in-distribution and does not directly test compositional generalisation. Several synthetic scaling and ablation results are reported as figure summaries or approximate ranges rather than exact per-condition values. The real-activation table aggregates across datasets, while per-dataset scores are separately shown in the table.
record.rows_left_out: Other synthetic results on latent recovery, dictionary learning, and downstream accuracy were not included because they are adjacent SAE/compositional-generalisation findings rather than measurements of the reconstruction residual or the specified claim versions. The paper's text also notes the limits of its real-LLM evaluation in Section 4.4.

untested.parts: No linear regression of SAE error on activations.
No per-token error norms or cross-size comparison of errors.
No spliced-in loss vs random-error comparison.
No circuit or steering analysis with or without the error term.
Compares SAE activation types on dictionary and latent recovery, not on reconstruction error or dark-matter size.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'/T6: the dark-matter paper is not cited, and reconstruction residuals are never measured. Table 3's caption appears mislabeled: it says Gemma-2-2B, but the text attributes those numbers to Pythia-70M.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether SAE error vectors are linearly predictable from input activations.
Does not measure per-token error norms or compare whether different SAE sizes fail on the same tokens.
Does not replace model activations with SAE reconstructions and compare the resulting model loss with matched random errors.
Does not decompose dark matter into linear and nonlinear components or test their feature-learning properties.
Does not test circuits or steering with and without the SAE error term.
Compares SAE types and inference procedures for latent recovery, but does not test whether dark matter is an SAE-training artifact or whether the dark-matter error shrinks with alternative training.

rows.subject: toy setting (synthetic data; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between learned decoder columns and the ground-truth dictionary.

conditions.value: SAE dictionaries; text reports an aggregate range, not separate type-specific values

rows.measure: Cosine similarity to ground-truth dictionary columns
rows.note: This measures dictionary direction alignment, not reconstruction-error structure.
rows.check: Dictionary cosine to ground truth in synthetic data; not a measure of SAE reconstruction error. The value ∼0.2–0.35 is at d_z=5000 for both SAEs and DL-FISTA, not SAEs alone. Ground-truth columns are the comparison target, not a baseline.

rows.subject: toy setting (synthetic data; model name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE encoding with per-sample FISTA on the same frozen SAE dictionary and FISTA warm-started from SAE codes.

conditions.value: SAE encoder, frozen-decoder FISTA, refined/warm-start FISTA; reported together

rows.note: The paper says the SAE-learned dictionary is the limiting factor; this is not a measurement of dark matter.
rows.check: MCC values ∼0.15–0.4 are reported for ID MCC (Figure 10 caption: 'bottleneck on ID MCC'), not OOD. Context is k=10, n=5000; d_z is varied across panels, not fixed at 5000. Latent recovery is not dark matter.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Trained logistic probes on each method's codes for eight text-classification datasets and evaluated held-out text; reports the mean over datasets.
rows.uncertainty: ± 0.06; table reports mean ± standard error over three seeds
rows.note: Adjacent downstream sparse-probing result; the text says DL-FISTA exceeds Top-K SAE on all eight datasets and raw-activation probes on six of eight.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (DL-FISTA) compared against others. It is a sparse-probing accuracy, unrelated to the SAE error term.
